mcq_fix.s: The basic structure doctrine is commonly traced to the constitutional jurisprudence of which country?
Which doctrine is used to reconcile apparent conflicts between Central and Provincial (State) laws by examining a law's true nature?
mcq_fix.why: oddly worded 'identified in an APPSC question'

mcq_drop.why: obscure case-by-case doctrine labelling; debatable (NCT Delhi/Joseph Shine split)

notes_fix.find: State List — 254(2): State law with President's assent prevails in that State
notes_fix.replace: State List — State law prevails within its field; Art. 254(2) (President's assent) applies only to Concurrent List matters
notes_fix.why: Art. 254(2) concerns Concurrent List laws, not State List

patterns: No PYQs filed here; APPSC G2 2017 asked only which doctrine reconciles Central and Provincial laws (pith and substance).
Likely APPSC shape: doctrine-meaning one-liners and case-to-doctrine pairs (Balsara, R.M.D.C.).
Traps: colourable legislation tests competence, not motive; Art. 254(2) applies to Concurrent List.
App goes into constitutional morality and transformative constitutionalism case lists, which is UPSC-level depth.
